newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African currency drifted weaker on Friday after taking a hit on robust dollar demand in early trade, despite subsequent efforts by the central bank to add liquidity into the market.

The rand was last at 4.5620/5650 against the U.S. currency from 4.5625/5655 at the local opening, compared to Thursday's 4.5530/60. Dealers said the central bank was active at various levels in the afternoon, but trade was thin.
Dollar demand was driven by position-squaring ahead of weekend in light two-way traffic. The range for early next week was seen between 4.55 at the base and 4.57 at the topside.
"For the moment, we are going to be a stuck in a tight range with bearish undertones to it," one dealer said.

The early dollar demand was broad-based, stemming from Europe, the Far East and an overflow of local demand from late Thursday. Importers were also active but the negativity was negated as exporters began buying at the top end.
"It was a very quiet afternoon session after the jab higher and straight back again in the morning," said one dealer.
"It all started with a bang but it's been very very quiet since," another added.

On the crosses, the rand was weaker against sterling trading at 7.6326/6399 from 7.6088/6184 late Thursday. The local unit was pegged at 0.3939/3942 on mark from Thursday's 0.3250/3255 and against yen, the rand was at 25.3721/3997 from 25.4970/5357.
On the bond market, light volumes helped to exacerbate the afternoon weakness as dealers showed a pre-weekend reticence to take a chance.

The benchmark R150 yield was pegged at 14.375 percent after opening at 14.34 percent compared to 14.30 percent late on Thursday. Although the market was lethargic in the afternoon session traders said the benchmark yield's downtrend was intact.
"It's been a fairly lacklusture market, not a particularly distinguishing day," one trader said.

"I expect the downtrend to continue in due course but like all markets it's got to take a breather and consolidate. All the fundamentals are still pretty positive -- although a big danger point of course is any undue slippage in the rand."
Gilts' short-term resilience was seen to be hamstrung by the currency's weakness, money market shortage and foreign sales of gilts of over 1.5 billion rand in the week so far.
The total value of Bond Exchange turnover was 44.75 billion rand on Thursday -- a settlement day -- from 5.5 billion rand on Wednesday.
Foreigners were net sellers of 552.41 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Thursday after selling 195.42 million rand on Wednesday, the Bond Exchange said.
On the money market, offered rates for three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.65 to 15.70 percent, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at 15.10 percent.
The South African Reserve Bank said the money market shortage rose to 9.732 billion rand on Thursday from 9.592 billion rand on Wednesday.
